_comment: The public Masinloc Connect Marketplace.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A LIVE QUERY
business_submissions lives in Supabase and predates this repository, so
there is no migration here describing it. More importantly there is no
public read path to it: the table has no anon SELECT policy, and the
columns a visitor may see have never been separated from the ones they may
not. Until it has that separation, a browser cannot be pointed at it without
risking owner_name, owner_email and owner_phone.
So this file carries only what a business asked to have published, entered
deliberately rather than queried indiscriminately. Approved-only holds by
construction: a row exists here because somebody put it here after it was
approved, not because a filter was applied correctly.
supabase/MARKETPLACE-LIVE-DATA.md describes what to deploy to move this to
a live feed, and what the page would then read.
NO PHONE NUMBERS, ANYWHERE
Both businesses submitted a mobile number and neither is published. The
public contact method is Facebook. The numbers are not held here at all —
not in a private key, not commented out — because a field that is absent
from the data cannot leak into a page, a script, a data attribute or a
JSON-LD block by mistake. contact and contact_number are in the generator's
FORBIDDEN list, so re-adding one fails the build rather than shipping.
Likewise owner_name, owner_email, owner_phone, reference codes, submission
ids, moderation status and dashboard-interest flags never appear here.
THE FACEBOOK LINKS ARE SHARE LINKS
Both are facebook.com/share/... URLs, which is what the businesses supplied.
They resolve to the right page, and they are published as-is. They are not
canonical Page URLs and nothing here describes them as such; rewriting one
into a cleaner-looking /pagename form would be inventing an address.
WHAT MAY AND MAY NOT APPEAR HERE
Public fields, matching what the edge function writes:
brand_name -> name, store_locations -> location,
short_description -> description, facebook_page -> facebook
'category', 'descriptor', 'schemaType' and 'metaDescription' have no column
behind them. They are editorial: how the business is classified, how it is
described in a search result, and which schema.org subtype is defensible for
it. They live here because a human decided them, not because a table did.
IMAGES
Logos are uploaded to masinloc-business-assets, which the edge function
creates with public:false. A public page cannot load them, and signing a URL
needs the service role. Neither business therefore carries an image, and the
cards are built to look deliberate without one rather than to show a broken
frame. See the runbook for the two ways to change that.
